10.1002_adfm.202531076: Aqueous iron‐sulfur (Fe//S) batteries are a promising next‐generation energy storage technology due to their high theoretical capacity and shuttling‐free mechanism. However, their development is hindered by dendrite growth, hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) at the anode, and low discharge voltage. Here, we address these challenges by pre‐constructing a polymer‑metal hybrid interphase on the Fe anode (polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF)‐M@Fe, M = Bi, Pb, Cu) to stabilize the electrode/electrolyte interface, while employing an electrolyte‐decoupling strategy (FeSO 4 /CuSO 4 ) to maximize the device discharge voltage through tailoring the charge carriers at the S cathode. Combining theoretical calculations with operando spectroscopy, we demonstrate that the outer PVDF layer effectively shields Fe anode from the bulk electrolyte, suppressing HER; while the inner electron‐conductive metal layer simultaneously homogenizes the electric field and increases nucleation sites, enabling dendrite‐free and highly reversible Fe deposition. This synergistic interface regulation allows a PVDF‐Bi@Fe symmetric cell to cycle stably for 412 h at 1 mA cm −2 . The decoupled PVDF‐Bi@Fe//S@activated carbon cell achieves a maximum discharge voltage of 0.85 V (2.4 times higher than that of the conventional cell), a large capacity of 1976 mAh g Sulfur −1 at a high rate of 2 A g Sulfur −1 , and remarkable cycling stability with 85.42% capacity retention after 100 cycles.
10.1002_adma.202518384: Sodium metal anodes (SMAs) are pivotal for high‐energy‐density batteries but suffer from uncontrolled dendrite growth and interfacial instability caused by infinite volume expansion and a fragile solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Herein, an innovative strategy is proposed, in which a p‐block matrix is in‐situ formed from NiTe 2 nanocrystals onto N‐doped carbon hollow microspheres (NiTe 2 @NC) during electrochemical activation to overcome these challenges. The p‐block matrix with sodiophilic Na 2 Te and conductive metallic nickel effectively reduces the nucleation barrier and establishes bi‐continuous ion/electron conduction networks, guiding uniform Na plating. Critically, Na 2 Te dominates the formation of a gradient inorganic‐rich SEI with high Young's modulus and low Na⁺ diffusion barrier, significantly enhancing mechanical resilience and ion transport kinetics. Consequently, the NiTe 2 @NC electrode achieves exceptional cyclability (1,000 cycles at 1.0 mA cm − 2 /1.0 mAh cm − 2 with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.79%). When configured in full‐cells with a Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 cathode, it maintains the capacity retention of over 96.1% (103.9 mAh g − 1 ) after 1,200 cycles at 10.0 C. Critically, the full‐cell maintains superior electrochemical resilience with high discharge‐capacity and >90% retention at low‐temperatures (−20 and −40 °C), demonstrating exceptional practicality for sodium metal batteries. This work establishes a new paradigm for stabilizing reactive metal anodes via in‐situ‐constructed multifunctional interfaces.
10.1007_s13753-026-00772-4: The Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), with rich cultural heritage, is increasingly exposed to climate-driven disasters, especially severe storm surges. This study develops a storm surge risk assessment framework for immovable cultural heritage under climate change, by coupling the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change hazard–exposure–vulnerability framework with Advanced CIRCulation (ADCIRC) model simulations. A total of 11,220 heritage sites were evaluated under 20-year and 100-year return period scenarios. Key findings include: (1) based on hazard simulation, the 100-year scenario inundated more sites (3587 sites, 31.97%) than the 20-year scenario (2413 sites, 21.51%), indicating higher storm surge inundation risk, with the greatest inundation depths in the central and western GBA. Hazard levels are relatively high in Foshan, Zhongshan, and Zhuhai. (2) Exposure is mainly associated with land use characteristics and shows clear spatial heterogeneity, with Guangzhou and Foshan showing relatively high exposure in both scenarios. (3) Vulnerability is generally moderate, and relatively high vulnerability is observed in Zhuhai, Huizhou, and Zhaoqing. (4) Integrated risk differs between scenarios: Guangzhou and Foshan show prominent risk under the 100-year scenario, whereas the proportion of high-risk sites decreases under the 20-year scenario, although Shenzhen and Dongguan still show relatively high within-city proportions of Levels I and II risk sites, and risk levels are associated with heritage protection grades. The findings suggest that the GBA should adopt a zoned and prioritized management strategy by improving disaster prevention in core priority zones and prioritizing resource allocation for high-risk, unclassified heritage units to prevent irreversible damage caused by intensifying storm surges.
10.1016_j.cej.2026.179961: The development of semi-solid-state batteries (SSSBs) requires gel electrolytes that simultaneously exhibit high ionic conductivity and excellent mechanical properties. We refined the gel-impregnated membrane (GIM) fabrication process by modeling gel crosslinking kinetics, enabling reproducible and scalable production of high-performance GIMs. We demonstrated that optimized crosslinking density is critical for achieving both high ionic conductivity and mechanical robustness. By correlating rheological properties, spectroscopic characteristics, conversion, and resistance of ionic conduction with gel crosslinking, we found that these properties collectively follow the Weibull kinetic model, providing a quantitative framework for predicting gel crosslinking density. This breakthrough enables systematic fabrication of gel electrolytes with controlled crosslinking. Through percolation analysis, we identified a critical monomer concentration of 4 wt% for gelation and confirmed that 5 wt% monomer content ensures Weibull kinetic behavior, leading to complete gelation in trimethylpropane ethoxylate triacrylate (ETPTA) system. The resulting GIM demonstrated no leakage, superior mechanical strength, and ionic conductivity exceeding 1 mS cm −1 , enabling stable SSSB operation. This study establishes a quantitative model for gel crosslinking, advancing the development of high-performance GIMs for next-generation solid-state batteries.
10.1038_s41467-026-78040-8: Layered oxide cathodes have attracted worldwide attention due to environmentally friendliness, structural diversity, and economic benefits. However, poor long-term cycling and unsatisfactory rate performance hinder the practical application. Hence, an oxide cathode with self-adaptive volume has been designed, achieving stable capacity retention of 82% after 1000 cycles at 2 C. The enhanced long-term performance is attributed to its dynamically adjustable volume reducing the acceleration of stress, enabled by a tunable interlayer distance that expands at the beginning of the charging process and then compresses at the highest voltage. Uniform electric field distribution is depicted by 4-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy showing even Coulombic interactions between the oxide layers leading to high mechanical integrity. Such self-adaptable behavior originates from the reduced repulsive force between interlayered oxygen due to the charge reconfiguration of intralayer oxygen and transition metal ions. Additionally, the charge compensation behavior is detected by in situ X-ray absorption spectra, which would be beneficial to high-rate performance. The self-adaptive volume change driven by charge reconfiguration provides a pathway toward durable materials for sustainable sodium-ion energy storage.
